paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God's warnings are not Him being mean. They are Him telling the truth before the trouble lands. In this passage the LORD says He will sling the people out of the land (Jeremiah 10:18), and He says why: the shepherds have become senseless, and "they do not seek the LORD" (Jeremiah 10:21). When the leaders stop seeking Him, the whole flock pays for it, and that's a heavy thing to see.

Now look at what the praying voice does with that. He says, "I know, O LORD, that a man's way is not his own; no one who walks directs his own steps" (Jeremiah 10:23). I think that's the most freeing sentence in the whole passage, because it means you were never supposed to run the map by yourself. Then he asks for correction, but "only with justice," and not in anger (Jeremiah 10:24). Friend, I flinch at a little feedback, so a person who asks for correction on purpose is somebody I want to learn from!

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery. Seek the LORD first, before the trouble shows up, because He's the one who can actually steer your steps. When correction comes, bring it to Him honestly, and trust that He knows how much you can bear. And when the world feels like it's devouring God's people (Jeremiah 10:25), the passage hands that to the LORD too, instead of asking you to carry it alone.
